2.text: him to take care of it, together with his own two boys. The prisoner, how-

3.text: ever, spent all his time sleeping in the shade, and left the boys alone with

4.text: the herd. Therefore, when it was time to carry meat to the house, the

5.text: slaughtered reindeer proved to be quite lean, without any trace of fat. The

6.text: master was angered at this, and asked the boys the reason of such a bad

7.text: condition of the herd. “It is because the assistant is very bad,” was the

8.text: answer. “Why in the world did you bring such a man here? He only sleeps

9.text: in the shade all the time, and, besides, he keeps thrashing both of us.”

10.text: The father came to the herd, caught the assistant sleeping, and gave

11.text: him a severe lesson with the aid of a heavy lash. Still the assistant continued

12.text: to do as before. In a few days the master came again and repeated the

13.text: thrashing, using this time a fragment of an iron chain. Then the assistant

14.text: changed his behavior. He began to be active with the herd. When the

15.text: herd ran, he ran still faster than the reindeer. They slaughtered a reindeer.

16.text: He said to the boys, “Now you may sleep.” He cut the meat and cooked

17.text: it, put it into a trough, then wakened the children. “Now, sit up and eat.”

18.text: The youths ate of the meat, put on their boots, and wanted to go to the

19.text: herd; but he said, “You may sleep again, I shall go to the reindeer.” The

20.text: boys slept as long as they wanted to; then they awoke and sat in the shelter,

21.text: singing. He became very careful, and was with the herd all the time. The

22.text: herd fattened. He became a good herdsman and very skilful in taking care

23.text: of the reindeer. They slaughtered again. The fawns were fat and round,

24.text: like a tallow candle. They slaughtered one young doe and two fawns. The

25.text: boys said, “Now you must go home and carry the meat.” He carried one

26.text: carcass on his back. When he came to the camp, the master was occupied

27.text: with some small handwork. “Oh, oh, you have come! There, give him

28.text: some dry boots to change with.” Thus he said to his wife. The master

29.text: untied the bundle, and saw the fawn-carcass quite white with fat. The heart

30.text: of the master felt merry. They ate of the fat meat. The assistant immediately

31.text: changed his boots again and wanted to go. “Where to?” — “To the herd!” —

32.text: “No, no, sleep here! Let the boys be alone.” They slept; but early in the

33.text: morning, when the master awoke, there was no trace of the assistant. He

34.text: had left for the herd. So the summer passed. They brought the kettles

35.text: home, and the fall slaughtering was about to begin. The assistant took so

36.text: much care of the herd, that the boys had no occasion to be with it. He

37.text: looked after it all by himself. The reindeer were quite fat. Their backs

38.text: were flat, like boards, and the old bucks were solid with meat.

39.text: The master felt thankful to the assistant; but there was treason in the

40.text: heart of the latter, and at last he succeeded in taking the master to a lonely

41.text: island far from the shore, and leaving him there. Then he came to the camp

42.text: and became master of it. For a few weeks he tyrannized over the boys and

43.text: the wives of the master, slaughtered the reindeer, and ate of the best. Eleˊndi,
